channel.description: Latest articles from The Alabama Baptist (thealabamabaptist.org)

item.title: Pisgah church host women’s conference
item.description: Freedom Baptist Church, Pisgah, will host a women’s conference, Made to Worship on March 7. Karmen Smith is the guest speaker with music provided by Erika Cookston Moyers. Brunch begins 9 a.m. followed by the conference at 10. The event is free. Dennis Johnson is pastor.

item.title: Creative evangelist Dan Bellamy captivates audiences with ‘blown-up stories’
item.description: For creative evangelist Dan Bellamy, balloons are more than decorations for a birthday party.

item.title: School prayer bills advance in 2 House committees
item.description: Two school prayer bills introduced by Rep. Reed Ingram, R-Pike Road, were approved in two Alabama House committees Wednesday (March 4).

item.title: Book review: New historical account of camp meetings contains rich detail, negative elements
item.description: Religious camp meetings were a notable part of American culture from the 1800’s, particularly so in Alabama and across the South.

item.title: Ten Commandments display bill advances in House committee
item.description: A bill requiring public schools to display the Ten Commandments in classrooms advanced Wednesday (March 4) without debate in the Alabama House Education Policy committee.

item.title: UM Grace Pilot School of Business Dean Kathy Dunning to retire; national search underway
item.description: The University of Mobile announced that Kathy Dunning, dean of the Grace Pilot School of Business, will retire at the conclusion of the 2025–2026 academic year. University officials have launched a national search for her successor.

item.title: Return of the neighborhood church? Rainer encourages ‘welcome and relationship.’
item.description: Evangelism is “the headwaters of everything,” according to pastor and ministry leader Sam Rainer. “All church health flows downstream from evangelism.”

item.title: Regular attenders aren’t joining your church? This may be why.
item.description: Maybe you know these people. They’ve been attending your church for some time — certainly long enough now to have decided whether to join officially.
